summary: Xiaomei and David meet for the first time and introduce themselves.

sents.en: Hello! My name is Xiaomei.
Hello, Xiaomei! My name is David.
Which country are you from?
I'm American. And you?
I'm Chinese.
Are you a student?
Yes, I'm a student. Are you also a student?
No, I'm a teacher.

t.g: to meet, to get to know

sents.en: Nice to meet you!

t.g: to meet, to get to know

sents.en: Nice to meet you too!

grammar.expl: 是 (shì) works like "to be" and links two nouns. Say 不是 for "am/is/are not".
Put 吗 at the end of a statement to turn it into a yes/no question. The word order stays the same.
也 means "also" and goes right before the verb.
呢 bounces a question back to the other person, like "And you?"

quiz.q: Where is David from?
What is Xiaomei's job?
What does 吗 do at the end of a sentence?

summary: A short description of a family of four and their cat.

sents.en: There are four people in my family.
Dad, mom, my older brother and me.
My dad is a doctor.
My mom is a teacher.
My older brother is twenty this year. He is a university student.
We also have a little cat at home.
It is very cute.
I love my family.

grammar.expl: 有 (yǒu) means "to have", and also "there is / there are".
Chinese puts a measure word between a number and a noun. 口 is used for family members and 只 for small animals.
Add 的 after a pronoun to show ownership. For close family, 的 is often left out: 我爸爸 "my dad".
Adjectives in plain statements normally take 很 in front. It is often weak and does not always mean "very".

quiz.q: How many people are in the family?
What does the older brother do?
What pet does the family have?

summary: Xiaomei orders a coffee and some bread.

sents.en: Hello! What would you like to drink?
I'd like a cup of coffee.
Do you want a large or a small cup?
A small one, thank you.
Would you like something to eat?
I'd like a piece of bread.
That's twenty-five yuan altogether.
Here is the money for you.
Thank you! Please have a seat.
Thank you!

grammar.expl: 想 means "would like to" and is polite. 要 is more direct and is common when ordering: "I'll have…".
还是 means "or" when you offer a choice in a question.
grammar.exEn: Do you want tea or coffee?

grammar.expl: 一共 means "altogether" and is used when adding up a price.
A question word such as 什么 simply takes the place of the answer. The word order does not change.
grammar.exEn: What would you like to drink?

quiz.q: What size coffee does Xiaomei order?
What food does she buy?
How much is the total?

titleEn: What Shall We Do This Weekend?
summary: Two friends plan a weekend walk in the park.

sents.en: Are you free this weekend?
Yes. What do you want to do?
I'd like to go for a walk in the park. The weather should be nice.
Sounds good! What time shall we meet?
Nine in the morning, at the entrance to the subway station.
Nine is too early. Is ten okay?
Okay. I'll bring fruit. What will you bring?
I'll bring my camera. We can take lots of photos.
That's great! See you at the weekend!

grammar.expl: 太…了 means "too…" (a problem) or "so…!" (delight).
几 (jǐ) asks "how many?" so 几点 asks "what time?". Answer with number + 点.
可以 means "may / can / is it okay to". It covers permission and possibility.
Repeating a verb (走走) makes the action short and relaxed: "just take a little walk".

quiz.q: Where will they meet?
What time do they decide on?
What will David bring?

titleEn: The Kitten Looks for a Friend
summary: A lonely white cat tries to make friends with a little bird.

sents.en: There was a little white cat that lived in a big house.
Every day it played alone. It had no friends.
One day, it saw a little bird outside the window.
"Hello! Can you play with me?" the kitten asked.
The bird said, "I'm a little afraid of you. Will you eat me?"
The kitten smiled. "I don't eat birds. I only eat fish. I want to be your friend."
The bird thought for a moment, then flew to the window.
From that day on, they played together every day.
The kitten was no longer alone.

grammar.expl: 了 shows that an action has been completed.
都 means "all" or "always" and goes before the verb.
不再 means "no longer / not any more".
从 + time + 起 means "starting from".
grammar.exEn: From today on, I will read every day.

quiz.q: Where does the cat live?
Why is the bird nervous at first?
quiz.a: It is afraid the cat will eat it

quiz.q: What does the cat say it eats?

summary: A busy worker describes a normal day from morning to bedtime.

sents.en: Every morning I get up at six thirty.
At seven I have breakfast. I often eat eggs and drink milk.
At eight I take the bus to work.
At noon I eat at a restaurant near the company.
I finish work at five in the afternoon.
After I get home, I cook, watch TV, and go to bed at eleven.
I feel that every day is busy, but I'm happy too.

grammar.pattern: Time words go before the verb
grammar.expl: In Chinese, time words such as 七点 or 中午 come before the verb, usually right after the subject.
在 + place says where the action happens.
Put 以后 after a time or an action to say "after…".
但是 means "but" and introduces the contrasting part.

quiz.q: What time does the writer get up?
How does the writer get to work?
What does the writer often have for breakfast?

summary: A traveller gets lost in Chengdu and is helped by a kind stranger.

sents.en: Last month I travelled alone to Chengdu.
That afternoon I wanted to go to a famous hotpot restaurant, but while walking I realized I was lost.
My phone had run out of battery, and I hadn't brought a map either.
I stood at the intersection, not knowing whether to go left or right.
Just then an old gentleman walked over and asked me with a smile, "Young man, do you need help?"
I told him I wanted to go to that hotpot restaurant. He thought for a moment and said, "Walk straight for two hundred meters, then turn right, and you'll see it."
I thanked him, followed his directions, and sure enough I found it very quickly.
The hotpot that evening was delicious, but what I remember most is still the old gentleman's smile.

grammar.expl: 着 after a verb shows an ongoing state or the manner of an action. Doubling it (走着走着) means "while walking along…".
往 means "toward". Use it with directions: 往左, 往前.
就 connects two actions and suggests the second follows soon or easily after the first.
grammar.exEn: Go straight and you'll see it.

grammar.expl: Besides "or" in questions, 还是 can mean "still / after all" in statements.
grammar.ex: 我最难忘的，还是他的笑容。
grammar.exEn: What I remember most is still his smile.

quiz.q: Why did the narrator get lost?
quiz.a: The phone had no battery and there was no map

quiz.q: What directions did the old man give?
quiz.a: Straight for 200 meters, then turn right

quiz.q: What did the narrator remember most?

summary: Someone who always ordered takeout learns to cook and discovers practice pays off.

sents.en: I never used to cook. Every day I ordered takeout.
Later I realized takeout was not only expensive but also not very healthy, so I decided to learn to cook myself.
The first time I made tomato and egg stir-fry, I put in too much salt and burnt the eggs as well.
My friend took a bite and said with a smile, "Not bad, just a little salty."
Now I have already learned to make more than ten dishes.
Although I can't really say I cook well, I love this feeling.
Cooking has taught me that as long as you practice more, everything gets easier and easier.

grammar.expl: "not only … but also …". It links two points that build on each other.
grammar.ex: 他不但会唱歌，而且会跳舞。
grammar.exEn: He can not only sing, but also dance.

grammar.expl: 把 moves the object in front of the verb to show what you did to it and what the result was.
grammar.exEn: I put in too much salt.

grammar.expl: "although … but …". Unlike English, Chinese normally uses both words.
越来越 + adjective means "more and more …".
grammar.exEn: The weather is getting colder and colder.

quiz.q: Why did the writer start learning to cook?
quiz.a: Takeout is expensive and not very healthy

quiz.q: What went wrong the first time?
quiz.a: Too much salt and burnt eggs

quiz.q: What did the friend say about the dish?
quiz.a: Not bad, just a little salty

summary: Over dinner, Xiaomei asks David to put his phone away.

sents.en: Why do you keep looking at your phone? We're eating!
Sorry, I'm replying to a work email.
It's rest time now. Work can wait until tomorrow.
You're right. I've been too busy lately. As soon as my phone rings, I want to look.
I'm like that too. So now when I eat, I put my phone in my bag.
That's a good idea. I'll try it too.
Then let's chat for a while first today.
Okay. Anything new with you lately?

grammar.expl: 怎么 can mean "how", but before a verb it often means "why / how come" and carries surprise or mild complaint.
grammar.exEn: How come you're not asleep yet?

grammar.expl: 在 before a verb shows the action is happening right now. 呢 at the end adds a "this is going on" feeling.
一 + verb … 就 + verb means "as soon as … then …".
grammar.exEn: As soon as he gets home, he sleeps.

grammar.expl: 再 means "again" or "(do it) later". It is used for future actions.

quiz.q: Why is Xiaomei unhappy with David?
quiz.a: He keeps looking at his phone during dinner

quiz.q: What is David doing on his phone?
What does Xiaomei do with her phone when she eats?
quiz.a: She puts it in her bag

summary: Tidying up, the narrator finds a letter from their grandmother and decides to call her.

sents.en: While tidying my room, I found an old letter in the bottom drawer of my desk.
The envelope had already turned yellow, but the handwriting on it was still clear. It was written to me by my grandma.

t.g: to be reluctant to part with

sents.en: Ten years ago, when I first left home for university in another city, Grandma was reluctant to see me go, yet she said nothing and just silently helped me pack.
The letter said: "Child, don't worry about home. Just study hard, and when you run into difficulties, believe in yourself."
As I read on, my eyes grew moist. All these years I have always been busy with work and rarely come home to see her.
I immediately picked up my phone and called Grandma.
At the other end of the line, her voice was as gentle as ever: "How come you suddenly thought of me?"
I said with a smile, "Grandma, this weekend I'm coming back to see you. I'll bring the pastries you love most."

grammar.expl: 是…的 puts the focus on who, when, where or how something happened. It is used for events that are already finished.
grammar.exEn: This letter was written by Grandma.

grammar.expl: 却 means "yet / however" and marks a contrast with what you would expect. It goes after the subject.
grammar.exEn: He's tired, yet doesn't want to rest.

grammar.expl: Repeating a verb with 着 means "while doing it… (something else happens)".
舍不得 means "to be reluctant to part with" or "to hate to do something".

quiz.q: Who wrote the letter?
How did the narrator feel while reading it?
What does the narrator promise at the end?
quiz.a: To visit this weekend and bring pastries

quiz.q: How long ago did the narrator leave for university?

summary: Tea is more than a drink in China: it shows respect, varies by region, and calms the mind.

sents.en: In China, tea is not just a kind of drink, but even more a way of life.
When a guest comes to someone's home, the host always pours a cup of tea first. This shows welcome and respect.
Different places like different teas. Southerners love green tea, northerners like jasmine tea, whereas Cantonese people are used to eating dim sum while drinking tea.
Research shows that drinking tea in moderation is good for your health, for example it can help people relax.
However, the greatest charm of tea may still be the kind of calm it brings.
So a cup of tea is often not just for quenching thirst.

grammar.expl: "not just … but even more …". It lifts a topic to a bigger idea.
grammar.ex: 这不只是工作，更是生活。
grammar.exEn: This is not just work, but a way of life.

grammar.expl: 边 + verb … 边 + verb means doing two actions at the same time.
grammar.exEn: He listens to music while walking.

grammar.expl: 比如 introduces an example: "for example".
grammar.exEn: I like fruit, for example apples.

grammar.expl: 而 contrasts two groups or ideas: "whereas".
grammar.ex: 他喜欢茶，而我喜欢咖啡。
grammar.exEn: He likes tea, whereas I like coffee.

quiz.q: What does pouring tea for a guest show?
Which tea do northerners like?
According to the article, what can tea in moderation help with?

summary: Xiaomei talks to a rental agent and negotiates the monthly rent.

sents.en: Hello, I'd like to rent a two-bedroom flat. May I ask whether there is one nearby?
Yes. This one is very close to the subway station, only five minutes on foot. It's 4,500 a month.
The price is a little high. Could it be a bit cheaper?
The landlord says that if you pay six months of rent at once, it can be two hundred yuan cheaper per month.
In that case it's 4,300 a month. I can think about it.
No problem. Would you like to go and have a look at the flat now?
Okay, sorry to trouble you to lead the way.

grammar.expl: 离 means "(distance) from". The pattern is A + 离 + B + distance word.
grammar.exEn: The school is very close to my home.

grammar.expl: Verb + 不 + Verb is another way to ask a yes/no question and offers both choices.
"if … then …". In speech 如果 is often dropped and 就 carries the meaning alone.
grammar.exEn: If it rains, we won't go.

grammar.expl: 一下 softens a verb: "do it for a moment / have a quick go".

quiz.q: Why might Xiaomei like the flat?
quiz.a: It is close to the subway

quiz.q: How can she get a lower monthly rent?
quiz.a: By paying six months at once

quiz.q: What would her monthly rent be then?

summary: An essay on why "slow living" appeals to young city dwellers and how to start.

sents.en: In recent years, "slow living" has become a topic that many young city dwellers talk about.
In a fast-paced society, people are chased by work and their phones every day, and have almost no time to stop and think about what they truly want.
So-called slow living does not mean doing nothing at all, but learning to leave a little blank space for yourself amid the busyness.
For example, walking home after work rather than squeezing onto the subway; on weekends turning off your phone, carefully cooking a meal, or chatting with your family.
These seemingly ordinary little things can make people feel the texture of life anew.
Of course, slowing down is not easy, because we have long been used to a way of thinking that puts efficiency above all.
But as long as we start with one small thing, perhaps we can slowly find our inner balance again.

grammar.expl: 被 marks the passive: the subject receives the action. The doer, if named, follows 被.
grammar.exEn: I got soaked by the rain.

grammar.expl: 并 before a negative word stresses a correction: "actually not / not at all".
"not A but B". 而不是 A means "rather than A".
grammar.ex: 他不是不想去，而是没时间。
grammar.exEn: It's not that he doesn't want to go; he has no time.

grammar.expl: "as long as … then …". It names the one condition that is enough.
grammar.exEn: As long as you work hard, you can succeed.

quiz.q: What does slow living really mean, according to the essay?
quiz.a: Leaving some blank space amid a busy life

quiz.q: Which example does the writer give?
quiz.a: Walking home instead of taking the subway

quiz.q: Why is slowing down difficult?
quiz.a: We are used to putting efficiency first
w: We have too much free time

quiz.q: What does the writer suggest at the end?

titleEn: A Story from the Night Market
summary: A tofu-pudding seller who never raises his prices gives a homesick customer a bowl he cannot forget.

sents.en: At six in the early evening, Old Zhou pushed his little cart to the night market as usual.
What he sold was the tofu pudding he made himself, only five yuan a bowl, and in twenty years he had never raised the price.
Someone advised him, "Everything has gone up in price now. You should raise yours a little too."
Old Zhou just shook his head: "The people who come are all familiar faces. If I raised the price, they'd feel too awkward to come."
That night, a young man stood in front of the stall for a long time.
He said that when he was little, every day after school his mother would bring him here for a bowl of tofu pudding.
Later he went abroad to work, and he hadn't been back in ten years.
Old Zhou was stunned for a moment, then handed him a steaming bowl of tofu pudding and said, "This bowl is on the house."
The young man lowered his head and took a mouthful, and his eyes suddenly turned red — the taste was, unexpectedly, exactly the same as in his memory.

grammar.expl: 像 A 一样 means "like / the same as A".
grammar.exEn: He got up early, as usual.

grammar.expl: 从没 + verb + 过 means "never (have done)". 过 marks past experience.
grammar.exEn: I have never been to Beijing.

grammar.expl: 竟然 expresses surprise that something is unexpected.
一下 means "briefly"; 一下子 means "all of a sudden".

quiz.q: Why has Old Zhou never raised his prices?
quiz.a: He doesn't want his regulars to feel awkward

quiz.q: What did the young man's mother do when he was little?
quiz.a: She took him for tofu pudding after school

quiz.q: How did the young man react after tasting it?
quiz.a: His eyes reddened because it tasted just like his memory
w: He complained it was too sweet
He asked for his money back

quiz.q: How long had the young man been away?

summary: An essay on the old streets and shops that quietly hold a city's collective memory.

sents.en: A city's memory is often not hidden in museums, but scattered in those unremarkable corners.
An old street shaded by plane trees, a tailor's shop that has been open for half a century, or an alley entrance from which the smell of soy milk drifts on some early morning.
However, as the pace of urban renewal keeps quickening, these spaces that carry collective memory are quietly disappearing.
Bulldozers roar past, leaving uniform high-rises behind, yet also wiping out the emotional coordinates shared by several generations.

Some believe this is the price development must pay; others argue that protecting old streets does not mean rejecting modernization, but letting the new and the old coexist harmoniously in the same soil.
How exactly to choose, I'm afraid, has no standard answer.
But we should at least realize that when the last old brick is taken down, what is lost is not only the building itself, but also the soul of a city.

grammar.expl: 随着 + a change introduces a trend that goes along with the result: "as / along with …".
grammar.ex: 随着天气变冷，人们穿上了厚衣服。
grammar.exEn: As the weather gets colder, people put on thick clothes.

grammar.expl: 意味着 means "to imply / to mean". 并不意味着 corrects a wrong inference: "does not necessarily mean".
grammar.ex: 努力并不意味着一定成功。
grammar.exEn: Working hard doesn't necessarily mean success.

grammar.expl: "not only … but also …", a bit more formal than 不但…而且….
grammar.exEn: He is not only smart but also hardworking.

grammar.expl: 恐怕 expresses a worried guess: "I'm afraid that …", usually about a bad outcome.
grammar.exEn: I'm afraid it will rain tomorrow.

quiz.q: Where does the essay say a city's memory often lies?
quiz.a: In ordinary corners such as old streets and small shops

quiz.q: What is happening to these spaces?
w: They are being rebuilt exactly as before

quiz.q: According to supporters of preservation, protecting old streets does not mean what?
What is lost when the last old brick is taken down?
quiz.a: The building and also the soul of a city

summary: A small act of kindness on a rainy evening stays with a woman for years.

sents.en: The rain started suddenly in the early evening.
She stood at the entrance of a bookshop, gazing at the hazy grey street, hesitating over whether to dash out into the rain.
"Use mine." An unfamiliar voice came from behind her.
A man with glasses held out a black umbrella, his expression calm, as if this were nothing more than the most ordinary of small matters.
She instinctively declined: "What about you?"
"My home is just across the street. Getting rained on for a few steps is nothing." Having said this, he turned and walked into the curtain of rain, and his back soon disappeared into the crowd.
In the many years that followed, she was never able to forget that umbrella, nor that moment when he turned away.
She wasn't sure whether it was love. She only knew that on that rainy day, a kind of warmth had quietly fallen into her life.

grammar.expl: 把 moves the object before the verb to show what is done to it and where it ends up.
grammar.exEn: He handed the book to me.

grammar.expl: 再 + adjective + 不过 means "it can't be more …": the most … there could be.
grammar.ex: 这是再简单不过的问题。
grammar.exEn: This is the simplest question imaginable.

grammar.expl: 仿佛 means "as if / seemingly" and is common in literary writing.
grammar.exEn: It was as if she heard the sound of rain.

grammar.expl: 始终 means "all along". 没能 + verb means "was unable to …" despite wanting to.
grammar.exEn: I was never able to get in touch with him.

quiz.q: Where was the woman standing when the rain began?
quiz.a: At the entrance of a bookshop

quiz.q: What did the man say about his home?
quiz.a: It was just across the street

quiz.q: How did he react when she asked, "What about you?"
quiz.a: He said it didn't matter and walked into the rain
w: He asked to walk with her

quiz.q: How does the woman feel years later?
quiz.a: She never forgot it and is unsure whether it was love
